purpose: Define one recoverable, provider-observed release lifecycle for Callisto so that a reviewed managed release merge automatically releases exactly its committed version, can be rerun safely after interruption, and never treats workflow structure or local state as proof of publication.
scope: The Callisto release domain model, graph coordinator, CLI, GitHub Actions adapter, binary assets, hermetic behavioral test harness, release documentation, and merge governance required before the next self-release.
non_goals: A second manual approval or a GitHub Environment reviewer gate.
Publishing a new version merely to recover an unpublished merged version.
Treating a local execution-state file as the authority for remote publication.
Apple Developer signing, notarization, or an owner-specific certificate before a project policy and safe credential model exist.
Inventing a staging registry endpoint, credentials, or external service that the owner has not provisioned.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A verified merge of a managed release PR is the only publication authorization; the release workflow contains no GitHub Environment assignment, required-reviewer gate, or equivalent second approval.

Release orchestration is modeled by a serializable run envelope (orchestration revision, release-source revision, intent digest, artifact-manifest digest -- no profile field; intent schema 5 removed it, matching SPEC-RELEASE-LIFECYCLE-HARDENING AC-001's 'no profile' requirement). It is derived from the intent by one constructor, validated across fields, and held in the in-memory execution state before the first effect; the receipt is built from it.

A recovery invocation accepts an explicit full release-source SHA, verifies it is an allowed merged managed-release commit, creates fresh intent and artifacts from that source, and does not invoke versioning or create a version PR.

The current Callisto CLI and workflow revision remain distinct from the checked-out release source during recovery; tests prove that a post-failure orchestration fix can recover an older unpublished release source.

All release lifecycle semantics--source validation, provenance, planning, observation, operation state transitions, terminality, receipt construction, and artifact-slot validation--have one CLI/graph owner; operation state changes only through a single pure transition table. Actions only supplies scheduling, isolated checkouts, artifact transport, credentials to execute, and command invocation.

Before every effect, on every run including a rerun, each registry publication, Git tag, forge release, forge publication, and artifact upload is provider-observed as absent, exact success (with typed per-role evidence), conflict, or indeterminate; conflict and indeterminate carry closed reasons and fail closed with typed diagnostics. Attempting is reachable only through an absent proof. Registry observation is `cargo info --registry` for crates.io (not the sparse index directly), the PEP 691 JSON simple index over curl for PyPI (not the /pypi JSON API), and `npm view` for npm; read-only observations use one bounded retry policy that honours Retry-After, effects are never blindly re-issued, and every outbound command has a deadline.

On every run, an exact pre-existing remote effect, a registry version included, is recorded as already satisfied without attempting a duplicate publication, with one warning line per adopted registry version; a same-identity version whose remote contents do not match the immutable intent is reported as a conflict. A yanked registry version reads as Absent, not Conflict (cargo's `cargo info` cannot see yanks; PyPI treats it as Absent by explicit choice), so it fails closed through a refused publish attempt rather than a Conflict diagnostic (matches SPEC-RELEASE-LIFECYCLE-HARDENING AC-014).

A run interrupted after any effect is completed by rerunning it on a fresh runner: execution state is in memory only and never persisted, so the rerun reconstructs progress from provider observations, adopts effects that already landed, and performs the rest; it cannot return success while any operation is incomplete.

A release receipt is emitted only after every required operation is provider-observed as terminal success or already satisfied, and the receipt is built from the in-memory execution state (run envelope plus the exact evidence each operation recorded), with no provider re-observation after the effects, and includes provenance and per-operation observation evidence.

[SUPERSEDED 2026-09-24 in part: the wasm32-wasip1 slot was removed with callisto-moon] The production release plan includes attested binary asset slots for aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, and wasm32-wasip1; the product-level GitHub Release is created as a draft, each validated asset is uploaded to the draft, and publishing the release is a separate last operation depending on every upload.

[UPDATED 2026-09-24: release profiles were removed] `[release].forge-repository` is the single destination authority consumed by the release lifecycle; a legacy production profile is migrated at config load, and any other profile name is rejected (matches SPEC-RELEASE-LIFECYCLE-HARDENING AC-026).

Executable behavioral tests cover fresh release, recovery, hidden and nested artifact transport, clean source worktrees, source/orchestration identity separation, partial provider success, provider conflict, and receipt emission; provider fakes serve captured real responses and reject flags outside the real tools' shapes, and emitted flags are checked against the real tools' help. Job-local Git credentials and no-secret plan/build jobs are verified only by the workflow-YAML policy and contract scripts (.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-contract.sh, verify-release-workflow-policy.sh), not by an executable behavioral test; line-oriented YAML checks remain only as narrow policy guards for those two properties.

[UPDATED 2026-09-24] Required status checks before merge are a GitHub branch-protection or ruleset setting, external to this repository's tracked files (.github/ holds only CODEOWNERS, templates, dependabot, workflows, actions, and scripts/tests; no ruleset is codified in-repo). The release workflow's verify job runs after merge, not as a merge gate. This criterion is verified manually against the repository's branch-protection settings, not from tracked files, while merge remains the sole release authorization boundary.

Documentation, CLI help, configuration examples, tests, and workflow behavior describe the same release lifecycle; obsolete preview-only release paths are removed rather than retained as a second implementation.

reasoning: Grounded in the owner-authoritative incident report and live source inspection on 2026-09-17. The owner explicitly rejected AWS and another distribution service for rehearsal, so external staging registry selection is deferred rather than fabricated.
